title: Missing or non-numeric confidence values can crash scoring during sort

finding.claim: Missing or non-numeric confidence values can crash scoring during sort
finding.evidence: The sort key coerces confidence with float(findings[i].get('confidence') or 0). If a reviewer returns a non-empty non-numeric confidence such as 'high', this raises ValueError before any scoring completes.
finding.recommendation: Parse confidence defensively, treating invalid values as 0 instead of raising. A small helper with try/except around float conversion would keep benchmark scoring robust against imperfect reviewer output.

probe.summary: Score-case probe (`probes/closingB_bench.py`, e8c5d3fd8a25 section): score_case (bench.py:226-231) converts a finding's recorded confidence with float(...). Confidence None → OK (matched counted). Confidence MISSING → OK. Confidence 'high' (a non-numeric string) → ValueError ('could not convert string to float') propagating out of score_case — a benchmark run over a record carrying a string confidence dies instead of scoring the case. Confidence 0.9 (control) → OK.
